method: independent second check; every stage read in full; numeric answers recomputed by script; encyclopedia titles verified against English Wikipedia; clinical ranges (vitals, ABG, anion gap, eGFR, HbA1c, potassium, qSOFA, FEV1/FVC, PaO2/FiO2, GCS) checked against standard values

corrections.at: all levels, all stages with missing or incomplete limits (51 stages: l1 s2-s8, l2 s1-s7 and s9, l3 s1-s9, l4 s1-s9, l5 s1-s9, l6 s1-s9)
corrections.what: limits was absent or did not say that patients are fictional and that this is not medical advice; added to every stage (level 1 wording: patients are made up, this is a game, not advice). Short stage-specific limits sentences were written where limits was missing entirely.

ordering item put 'immune system fights back' after 'symptoms'; symptoms are partly caused by the immune response, so the order was arguable. Reordered to: germ enters, multiplies, immune system responds, symptoms may appear; why updated.
'Medication safety' is not an English Wikipedia title; replaced with 'Medical error'
'Clinical reasoning' does not exist; replaced with 'Medical diagnosis' and prompt reworded to match the article
'ABCDE approach' does not exist; replaced with 'Advanced trauma life support'
'Sequential organ failure assessment' does not exist; replaced with 'SOFA score'

needsSpecialist.what: SpO2 88 percent on room air is keyed as low and needing urgent attention for a general fictional adult; some chronic lung disease patients have lower target ranges (88 to 92 percent), but the question states no such condition. Fine as a general item; a clinician may wish to confirm the wording.
